arms.description: E = 0.45(1 - thr) + 0.35 clip((aspd - 12)/8) + 0.20 batt; dS = mean of capped predictor and nav residuals; dC = 0.45 osc + 0.25 sat + 0.20 low + 0.10 conf; U = E - 0.7 dS - 0.7 dC; hold when U <= -0.75 for 3 s
arms.name: isrm_gated_hold

arms.description: hold when the PID health score (0.25 alt + 0.20 aspd + 0.20 xtrack + 0.15 low + 0.10 sat + 0.10 conf, with integral and derivative terms) >= 1.35 for 3 s
arms.name: pid_gated_hold

arms.description: PID alarm with 3 s dwell and hysteresis, no ISRM channels
arms.name: pid_dwell_only

environment.name: energy_limited_plant
environment.status: to be implemented: second-order airspeed/altitude plant with throttle-limited energy, engine-multiplier disturbance steps, mission completion scored

hypothesis_h0: The two gates are within +/-5% on throttle integral and alarm burden; a 3 s dwell on the PID alarm alone removes >= 25% of alarms; ISRM's channels add no lead time.
hypothesis_h1: On an independent energy-limited plant with engine-multiplier steps, an ISRM-gated hold (U <= -0.75 sustained 3 s) reduces the recovery throttle integral by at least 10% relative to a PID-score-gated hold (score >= 1.35 sustained 3 s) at equal mission completion.
metric: recovery throttle integral as a fraction of the no-intervention run (lower is better)
notes: Mission completion must be scored; the original benefit coincided with abandoning the mission (100% LOITER in recovery).
source_claim: Recovery-phase PID alarm burden 19.2-32.1% (ACTIVE) vs 62.6-66.3% (SHADOW); throttle integral in the energy deficit not reduced (5664.7/7318.2/5594.1 vs 5653.3/5554.2/5675.9 %-s); the only intervention was a sustained CONSERVE_CRITICAL LOITER after which the mission was never resumed.
title: ISRM sidecar over PID: ISRM-gated hold vs PID-score-gated hold on a synthetic energy-limited plant
